WASHINGTON: The Republican-led US House of Representatives moved on Tuesday (Nov 10) to effectively block an effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, buying more time for the polarising Pentagon chief before Democrats take control of Congress next year and possibly try again. The vote on a procedural motion came just hours after Hegseth blasted efforts to impeach him as a farce and delivered a defiant defence of his record at the helm of the Pentagon, winning praise from President Donald Trump. Republicans passed a motion to refer eight articles of impeachment to the Judiciary Committee, a move that the sponsor of the impeachment push, US Representative Thomas Massie, warned would kill it. Massie, an outgoing Kentucky Republican, hoped to draw votes from Republicans upset with Hegseth's policies and wary of the unpopularity of the Iran war. Democrats had voiced strong support for the impeachment effort and they tried to help Massie clear the way for an impeachment vote.

Hegseth would have been the first US defence secretary to be impeached. The last time any civilian leader of the US military was impeached was in 1876, when William Belknap held the title "secretary of war". Hegseth calls himself secretary of war, part of his effort to rebrand a military he said was too weak and "woke" when he took office last year. Trump cannot change the name of the Defense Department without approval from Congress.

Related:

IRAN WAR ANGER Voter anger over the Iran war, which has settled into an effective stalemate focused on securing the Strait of Hormuz, helped Democrats win control of Congress in last week's midterm elections. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries took aim at Hegseth ahead of the vote, saying on Monday: "Pete Hegseth has abused his power, undermined America's national security, and he's the architect of the reckless and costly failed war of choice in Iran." But Hegseth repeatedly defended the conflict, calling Trump courageous and saying Iran's military has been left in ruins. He also said his orders to US forces were lawful, despite Massie's accusations of "high crimes and misdemeanours" ranging from the war itself to the US military raid in January to depose Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro. "History will judge the Iran war quite differently than the conventional wisdom right now," he said. Trump repeated his backing of Hegseth in a post on his Truth Social platform just after the Pentagon briefing ended. "Pete Hegseth gets an 'A' PLUS, PLUS, PLUS for his defence against a disgruntled, angry, defeated, former Congressman, Thomas Massie, a TOTAL LOSER!" he wrote.

Source: Reuters/fh

Israeli President Isaac Herzog urged lawmakers to "do everything to avoid another election”.

JERUSALEM: Israel 's parliament was sworn in on Tuesday (Nov 10) without a new government , after a deadlocked general election stripped Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his parliamentary majority but left his main rivals with no clear path to power. Lawmakers elected in the Oct 27 vote took their oaths of office as Gadi Eisenkot , a former general, sought to forge a coalition after Israel 's president tasked him on Sunday with forming a government . Eisenkot and his allies also lack a majority and he has yet to strike deals with parties that could bring him to power. If both Eisenkot and Netanyahu fail to form coalitions, another election could follow. Presiding over the swearing-in ceremony, President Isaac Herzog told lawmakers: "You must do everything to avoid a repeat election."

"Reach out a hand for compromise, even between rivals ... Look upon one another with generosity. There is much work to be done here, and it requires the ability and experience found in every part of this House."

PARLIAMENT COULD TRY TO SET UP OCT 7 INQUIRY Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister until a new candidate manages to form a coalition. His right-wing Likud party's alliance with far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties outperformed election expectations but still lost its majority, now holding 53 of the Knesset's 120 seats. Eisenkot's centre-right Yashar party and patchwork partner factions hold just 48 seats. But they have potential allies in Israel 's Arab-led parties, which hold 19 seats and are aligned with Eisenkot in their vehement opposition to Netanyahu . This means that the newly sworn-in parliament could still deliver on some of Eisenkot's campaign promises, such as potentially setting up a commission of inquiry into the Oct 7, 2023 Hamas attacks, something backed by the Arab parties but largely opposed by Netanyahu . It also could allow Eisenkot to replace the current Knesset speaker, a Likud member. Herzog told Knesset members that parliament was "duty bound to leave no stone unturned" in investigating and understanding the "catastrophe" of Oct 7, while Israel continues to face threats from Iran and its proxies. Eisenkot initially has until Dec 6 to form a government but he can seek a two-week extension to Dec 20. He has acknowledged his path to power is "extraordinarily complex". His options include trying to form a minority government with Arab party support, bringing ultra-Orthodox parties into his camp despite years of mutual hostility, or forging a unity government with Netanyahu . All three paths face formidable obstacles. Ultra-Orthodox parties have so far said they would not join an Eisenkot-led government .

Related:

For his part, Netanyahu has cast doubt on the election results by baselessly alleging voter fraud by Arabs, who make up a fifth of the population. Election officials have said they are probing potential misconduct, but that they have seen no evidence of fraud that could have influenced the vote's outcome. Speaking after parliament was sworn in, Netanyahu called for a unity government , warning that Iran was seeking to revive its nuclear programme and that Israel could come under growing international pressure to accept a nuclear-armed Iran. "Only such a (unity) government will be capable of confronting challenges of this magnitude," he said. If Eisenkot fails to form a government , Herzog would likely ask Netanyahu to try to build a coalition. If he also fails, another candidate would get a chance before Israel would be forced into another election. Moments after the official opening of parliament, Eisenkot and his allies submitted a series of bills, including legislation to establish a state commission of inquiry into the Oct 7 attacks and to impose term limits on the prime minister. They also proposed repealing a controversial judicial overhaul and other laws enacted under Netanyahu 's government over the past four years. Among those sworn in on Tuesday was Elisha Madan, a military reservist who lost both legs fighting in Gaza. He received a standing ovation from lawmakers as he rose on his prosthetic legs to take the oath of office.

Source: Reuters/fs

GENEVA: The Un ited States spurned a UN meeting on Tuesday (Nov 10) where its human rights record un der US President Donald Trump was due to be examined, drawing criticism from rights groups who say violations have surged to levels not seen in decades. Washington disengaged from the Geneva-based UN Human Rights Co un cil last year, citing an anti-Israel bias, and this is the second year in a row that it has skipped its own review - a process that even authoritarian state s take part in. The US left its seat on the stage of the UN meeting empty and the council decided to postpone the event until January. A US State Department spokesperson said participation would imply endorsement of the co un cil's work.

"This irredeemable body makes a mockery of human rights through consistent failures to uphold its own 'values' as it p us hes anti-American rhetoric," the spokesperson said, without responding to allegations about the US record. The 47-member co un cil has not directly criticised Washington's rights record but its appointed experts have, such as over migrant deportations. Washington said deportations wer e carried out in accordance with US immigration law.

QUESTIONS ON ABORTION AND DEATH PENALTY The Un iversal Periodic Review asks all 193 UN member states to submit a rights report every few years and these are review ed by other states , which provide non-binding recommendations. UN documents show co un tries had planned on Tuesday to raise issues such as abortion and the death penalty. US and international non-governmental organisations also sent nearly 200 UN submissions covering topics from migration to racial discrimination. “We've seen attacks on f un damental human rights and civil liberties un precedented in generations," Jamil Dakwar , of the American Civil Liberties Un ion , told reporters in Geneva. "Enough is enough." Fourteen co un tries are due to take part in the review process in Geneva this month. In Trump's first term in office, the US submitted its UPR report. Noor Abdalla, wife of pro-Palestinian student activist Mahmoud Khalil, who was held in immigration detention last year, is among campaigners pressing UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk to promptly hold a briefing on the US rights situation, even in Washington's absence. "When the most powerful government in the world is not held acco un table, they think that they can do whatever they want," Abdalla told reporters. However, diplomats were sceptical given that few states want to confront Washington. "The view is to leave the door open and hope they come back in two years," said a diplomat.

WASHINGTON: Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday (Nov 10) blasted efforts to impeach him as a farce that would embolden US adversaries, as he lashed out at his political opponents in Congress and the media in an unapologetic defence of his record. Striking a defiant tone at a Pentagon news briefing, Hegseth thanked US President Donald Trump for his continued support as the House of Representatives scheduled a procedural vote for late Tuesday that will test support for his impeachment. Hegseth said past impeachments of Trump had ultimately failed, and added: "Both times he came back stronger, and the American people sent him back to the White House. Now they're trying a third time. This time against a member of his cabinet." US Representative Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, introduced eight articles of impeachment against H egseth on Monday. Massie said in a post on X that if the House of Representatives can overcome Tuesday's procedural effort, "we will proceed to a real debate and vote on the Articles of Impeachment".

Congressional sources say the resolution may have the votes to pass even with Trump’s Republicans still controlling the House until Democrats take over on Jan 3. Conviction appears unlikely in the Senate, however, where a two-thirds majority is required and Republicans hold 53 of 100 seats. Hegseth is accused of various abuses of power in office, including issuing orders to go to war with Iran without an imminent threat or approval from Congress. Voter anger over the Iran war helped Democrats win control of Congress in last week's midterm elections . A new Reuters/Ipsos poll published on Tuesday found a majority of Americans want the newly elected Democratic-majority US Congress to act to end the war with Iran.

US Representative Thomas Massie holds a press conference about his resolution to impeach Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth, on Capitol Hill in Washington, DC, on Nov 9, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Evelyn Hockstein)

Vice President JD Vance has publicly questioned the war. Hegseth declined to be drawn into responding to Vance, but defended the conflict, calling Trump courageous and saying Iran's military has been left in ruins. "History will judge the Iran war quite differently than the conventional wisdom right now," he said. Hegseth cited US Secretary of State Marco Rubio as saying of the war: "It's not necessarily popular, but it may have been necessary, and that's certainly how I feel. It was a necessary undertaking." Trump repeated his backing of Hegseth in a post on his Truth Social platform just after the Pentagon briefing ended. "Pete Hegseth gets an 'A' PLUS, PLUS, PLUS for his defense against a disgruntled, angry, defeated, former Congressman, Thomas Massie, a TOTAL LOSER!" he wrote. A polarising figure in American politics, Hegseth would be the first US defense secretary to be impeached. The last time any civilian leader of the US military was impeached was in 1876, when William Belknap held the title "secretary of war". Hegseth, a former Fox News host, calls himself secretary of war, part of his effort to rebrand a military he said was too weak and "woke" when he took office last year. But even some Republicans say his strained relations with Congress are becoming a political liability as the administration seeks a US$1.5 trillion defense spending package. In a possible nod to the spending requests, Hegseth said Republicans should use their final weeks in control of Congress to deliver wins for the American people instead of pursuing his impeachment. If he's still around next year, Democrats have promised to investigate Hegseth and his handling of the Pentagon, including his firing of the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and other top military officers.

The US is looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who is an alleged spy and a former executive at Megaspeed.

SINGAPORE: Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed faces renewed scrutiny as the United States looks into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang , alleged to be a spy for Beijing . Here are details of Megaspeed, where Huang used to be an executive. WHAT IS MEGASPEED? Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer, was incorporated in 2015 as 7Road International before changing its name to Megaspeed International in March 2023, its business filings showed. It is wholly owned by Singapore-registered Swiftdata incorporated in October 2023, which says providing hosting services by non-data centres is its principal activity.

Two Singapore citizens are listed as officers of both companies. Tan Yong Pong was appointed a director of Swiftdata on Oct 31, 2023, before becoming a director of Megaspeed less than two weeks later. The same month, Huang Le ended an eight-month tenure as managing director of Megaspeed, media said. Huang Le is Alice Huang's Chinese name. Swiftdata also shares an address with Ng Wei Shi Khloe, who is listed as company secretary of both companies. Tan and Ng are the only listed officers of the two firms in their business filings. Reuters could not immediately contact Swiftdata, and Megaspeed did not respond to a request for comment. Megaspeed has faced US scrutiny over suspicions that it helped Beijing gain access to Nvidia's advanced AI chips whose export to China is restricted. On its website, it says it is an Nvidia Cloud Partner in the Asia-Pacific region and offers access to the company's GB200 NVL72 and HGX H100 systems. Megaspeed's assets increased sharply to US$3 billion in 2024 from US$33 million in 2023, its business filings showed. It reported after-tax loss of US$20 million in 2024, versus a loss of US$21,283 a year earlier, while revenue jumped to US$294 million from zero. Its cashflow statement showed US$844,555 went to investing activities in 2024, after financing activities brought in cash of US$10 million the previous year.

Related:

From affair allegations to Nvidia probe: How the Jensen Huang controversy unfolded

Who is Alice Huang, Chinese exec accused of spying on Nvidia CEO?

SINGAPORE'S ROLE Last October Singapore police said they were investigating Megaspeed over "suspected breaches of our domestic laws" after a US senator requested the Commerce Department to investigate whether Megaspeed had diverted Nvidia chips. Last month, the home affairs ministry responded to remarks in the Wall Street Journal that Singapore was concerned about Alice Huang's ties to Jensen Huang, with authorities separately investigating her alleged links to Chinese intelligence. "We would like to make clear that neither the Singapore Government nor its officials said this. And there were no such investigations conducted in respect of Alice Huang," it said, while adding that investigations into Megaspeed continue. The ministry did not immediately respond to a request for further comment on Tuesday. Singapore has become a key site for Chinese firms to set up offices in recent years, in efforts to "Singapore-wash", or domicile in the trade-focused country to reduce risks from China-US tensions. Singapore has said it does not enforce "unilateral export controls imposed by other countries", but it acts "firmly against companies and individuals who violate our laws and are engaged in fraudulent and dishonest practices". It is currently investigating four other individuals charged with chip fraud in an unrelated case.
